architecture.summary: Stream stdin-free local file path through bounded binary/gzip input, strict csv.reader with record-span capture and cap, operator-supplied versioned schema validator, exact decimal accumulator, and staged CSV writers plus JSON reconciliation. Commit is a separate durable marker after all output files are complete; no completed artifact is authoritative without marker. A single sequential process and explicit injected filesystem, clock and progress seams avoid synchronization complexity, support deterministic tests and prevent expanding memory with total row count.
interfaces: CLI main.py --input PATH --output DIR --schema POLICY.json --batch-size N --max-record-bytes N --on-record-error reject|fail; status exit=0/2/1 under documented design.
ByteSource => iterator of bounded physical line bytes; gzip stream decompression in chunks, Unicode decode with explicit encoding; strict CSV parser yields logical record with physical span.
Validator accepts explicit immutable SchemaConfig + candidate string columns; returns AcceptedTransaction or RejectedRecord(code, location, raw if available); never mutates original fields.
Accounting ledger counts examined, accepted, rejected and exact amount per currency; only completed file runs enforce examined == accepted + rejected.
Output sink writes validated.csv and rejected.csv to private attempt staging files; final summary.json and COMMITTED.json published on successful or fully read partial-with-rejections completion.
Dependency seams: FileSystem(open/replace/fsync) protocol, Clock(time/monotonic), EventSink(progress), RawSource, CsvWriter; tests inject handwritten concrete implementations.

Batching is capped by BOTH configurable record count (target default 10000) AND a separate maximum aggregate buffered byte budget; if even one row exceeds the cap, fail before retaining it; do not allocate 10000 maximum-sized rows.

The decompression/byte reader reads fixed-size chunks and detects maximum physical line/record length BEFORE creating unbounded line/text strings, never relying on unbounded file.readline or naive gzip iteration.
failure_modes: Unbalanced quotes/unknown headers/unrecoverable decoder or gzip CRC/trailer => fatal FAILED no final marker and count observed progress only.
Invalid row of a valid shape (malformed amount/timestamp/currency) => reason-coded rejection with raw source fragment where recoverable; stream continues when safe.
Oversized field/physical or quoted-multiline record must fail safely before exceeding the configured bound, not truncate, skip, or wrongly concatenate.
Disk exhausted, error writing, file collision, duplicate output directory, termination, kill, or failed fsync => no authoritative committed marker; diagnostic best-effort only.
If commit-marker write fails after files renamed, outputs are not approved; rerun makes a new attempt or refuses overwrite; marker is last and sole sign of success.

Coverage-first early increments may report expected nonpass for frozen end-to-end tests before features exist; Codex records actual failures rather than skipping frozen acceptance or declaring the early gate passed. No advanced assurance until the complete source scope and frozen suite pass.
security_boundaries: Never transmit input, output or telemetry externally; process only local paths with read/write permissions, redact stdout/stderr account and amount content.
Protect staging/results with restrictive umask and directory/file permissions; avoid symlink path traversal and risky input/output aliasing.
No user-controlled CSV formula sanitization that changes financial data; warn consumers that spreadsheets may execute formula-looking text.
No real transaction data in generator/test; secrets only in local protected output files and never stack-trace dumps.
